- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 2–3% below true peak or adjust downward 1–2 days after spike.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.5) and price is trending up, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- Model frequently underestimates in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or negative — apply slight upward bias for short-term (1–3 day) forecasts.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model lags in adjusting — forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For long-term (10+ day) forecasts, model tends to overfit recent trends; apply mean reversion by subtracting 0.5–1.5% from forecast if recent price movement is >2% above 30-day moving average.
- If sentiment is high and price is rising, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 2–3 days to avoid over-optimism.
